utterances.text: Now, sir, let's try and illustrate this. If you cannot establish some sort of communication, then at that time from the communications centre you have no indication of the reason the lines were down, the communication was down?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, mostly no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So there were various possibilities. Perhaps there was no electricity in the area, that's one possibility, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then there's another possibility. For example, one -- the reception equipment was down; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Then there's another possibility. There might have been a physical interruption to communications; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then there's also the possibility of the communication lines being overused and not enough capacity?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. And there was also combat going on where the phones would be ringing but nobody would answer, and then when they did answer they would say that they were in a shelter. So that was another possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in addition to the keys for decoding, there were plans as well, documents called plans, for establishing communication; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And those plans were limited for security reasons. They had a dead-line, just as the keys did, they had a life span?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, in addition to other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So, for example, if at a given point in time you provided the keys for decoding and the plan for establishing communications, which covered a period of, say, one month, after that month had expired you are unable to supply a new set of documents, then you were facing a serious problem again; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now I'd like to show you a number of documents for us to illustrate this communication between the CBS [as interpreted] and the communications centre of MUP at its headquarters. It is a fact, is it not, that there were five security services centres on the territory of Republika Srpska, the MUP of Republika Srpska I mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: They were Banja Luka, Doboj, Bijeljina, Sarajevo, and Trebinje; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now may we see document 65 ter 955, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's a bulletin of daily events, one of them, shown to you by Mr. Hannis. I know that you said you didn't receive anything like that, but what I'm interested in basically is just a comment at the very end of this daily bulletin or report. And the date of it is the 15th of May, 1992, signed by the service for information of the ministry where it says: "On the territory of the CSB of Bijeljina there were no especially interesting events security speaking ..." And at the -- do you see that final paragraph there: "There were no incidents of particular security interest in the area of Bijeljina CSB ..." Now, I assume -- I assume that that means that at that point in time there was no communication between the communications centre of the ministry at its seat and the CSB of Doboj and Banja Luka, or rather, Trebinje; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For one of the reasons that you enumerated earlier on most probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now may the witness be shown 65 ter 956 next, please, page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is another daily bulletin or report. The following day, the 16th of May, 1992, the information service once again, and at the bottom it says: "So far the Bijeljina, Doboj, and Trebinje CSBs have not submitted their daily reports." And I assume that the reason for that was the same, that there was no communication; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is very possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now may the witness be shown 65 ter 957, please, page 2 again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a document, once again a bulletin or a report, dated the 18th of May this time, and once again those three CBS centres, Trebinje, Doboj, and Bijeljina failed to submit reports on daily events or incidents. I assume that your answer will be the same as to the reason that there was no communication; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, in normal situations in the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that was also true for the MUP of Republika Srpska, the CBS, the security services centres, are duty-bound to send in daily reports to the MUP at its seat; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, here we have a situation that is different, looking at those two documents. Of the five centres, three were not sending in reports, and that's a highly irregular situation, is it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to show you document 65 ter 270, and I'm going to ask you for your comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I wonder if I could be assisted by my friends from the Prosecutor's side. I was notified that the documents which I read, 65 ter 955, 956, and 957 have not been exhibited.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I'm sorry. Those are on the list of daily reports that I wanted to tender. I don't think they've been assigned a number yet because they're part of that group of 15 or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's perfectly all right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're not receiving the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe that there was no interpretation in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, could you just repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. I said that those are on the list of daily reports that I wanted to tender. I don't think they've been assigned a number yet because they're part of that group of 15 or so that we provided to the Registry officer by e-mail just a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And just for the purposes of interpretation, I said: Thank you, it's appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, sir, this is a letter sent to the Ministry of the Interior on the 7th of May, or rather, the date is the 7th of May, 1992, and it is signed by Predrag Jesuric. Now, what I'm interested is this, the first paragraph which says, and I'll help you out because it's rather a poor copy so I'll read it out. "Due to a break in the telephone, telegraph, and fax communications, during the period from the last report you did not receive reports, although they were compiled by the chief of the Bijeljina CSB, security services centre." Now, it is a fact, is it not, that Bijeljina - and we saw this on the basis of some previous documents - was for a time left without any communication with Pale; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We can then indubitably conclude from this that this lasted for some time because he speaks of reports, in the plural.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I can also tell you that it was mostly because of power outages, in Bijeljina especially. And the building in Bijeljina, that of the municipal secretariat, was the last one to be built and put into operation. It was built according to all the proper standards. It even had a power generator for the entire building, but it didn't help. If you just tried to ignite a car 100 times a day by pushing the car, it's impossible. It was simply impossible to find a moment during the day when everything was working properly. There were days like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I heard you saying that it was impossible to find a half-hour during the day when everything was working to actually send and receive?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because the whole process of re-typing dispatches and all that you described before takes a couple of hours. And if you interrupt it for some reason midway, you have to start all over again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I just want to ask you if this document is known to you or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I personally don't know about it because it was not addressed to me or ever made available to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is no objection, for the sake of completeness of this testimony, I would like to offer this document to be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: This isn't a part of the -- okay. So marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D234, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Just to illustrate this situation further, can I show the witness 1D00-2978. I would like page 2 first in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is an undated document, unfortunately, but judging by what is written there I would say it's from May/June, possibly, 1992. And it comes from the Zvornik public security station. It says "report on the situation ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 3, please. Page 3 in Serbian and page 2 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you see in paragraph 1 on this page it says: "One difficulty in our work is the communications system which could be used to communicate between reserve police stations and neighbouring municipalities. Telephone communications almost throughout the municipality are down. Radio communication can be used only at smaller distances because the repeater is broken down."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, it should be page 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And in brackets: " ... (there is only one fixed, two on wheels," I suppose that means cars, "and two Motorolas)." And then it goes on to speak about other technical equipment. Do you remember that at that time in 1992 at the level of public security stations too such problems were experienced throughout Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, especially Zvornik was in a difficult situation and some more municipalities like Milici and Vlasenica because they belonged to the Tuzla region and they were connected through the PTT and other lines directly to Tuzla. So something had to be changed dramatically in the state for them to be reconnected to someone else. First the telecom had to do it and then the police had to join in with their capacities. Now, if somebody's holding or controlling transmitters and radio relay installations, that would have been very difficult to effect that change. It's not perhaps across the board what I'm describing, but it was different in every municipality, every region. Only Banja Luka was fortunate in that respect, that all of their municipalities in Doboj remained connected to them, of course with all the accompanying problems like power outages, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So all this eastern part of Republika Srpska, municipalities of Vlasenica, Milici, Zvornik, I suppose Bratunac as well, they were all connected to the PTT node, the switchboard in Tuzla, which was controlled by the Muslims. And that is why no kind of communication with them was possible?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the outset, that's how it was. Bijeljina, Brcko, Ugljevik, Lop are, the entire north-eastern part from Zvornik on was connected to Tuzla. After Sarajevo it was probably the largest region by the number of municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that part of the communications with Eastern Bosnia and north-Eastern Bosnia resumed practically only in the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say that. Some transitional solutions were found, but they were really transitional. There was something, but absolutely substandard.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document to be marked for identification if there is no objection by Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection to MFI. I know there's no date or signature or name on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D235, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown P589.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a letter from the CSB Sarajevo dated 25 July 1992, and you can see on page 1 the second sentence, indicating how serious the situation is. It says: "The most frequent problem in the preparation of data is weak communication with public security stations as a result of war operations." Since Sarajevo was not far from Pale, are you aware that the security services centre and their chief, Mr. Zoran Cvijetic, experienced difficulties in communications and establishing contact with the public security stations subordinate to them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's precisely what we were discussing before. They were at Vrace at the outset and then they moved to Lukavica, and they moved from Lukavica mainly because communications were impossible to establish.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This move from Lukavica - because it was impossible to establish communications and make contact - also happened in the end of summer 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can see the time and I would like -- perhaps it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Could we please have 1D176.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kezunovic, it is a fact, isn't it, that as you said at the beginning, that Mr. Stanisic gave you a carte blanche in the sense that you were allowed to create a fully functioning communications system within the MUP of the RS; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And it is also a fact, is it not, that Mr. Stanisic supported you in that, he met every request of yours that he could in terms of equipment and similar things; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You're probably familiar with the fact that the minister insisted on constant, daily exchanges of information; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: To illustrate that, I wanted to show you 1D176, which is an order of the minister dated the 27th of July, 1992. Let's go to item 9 on page 2 in both versions, please. Item 9. I don't know how well you can read this on the monitor. In essence, the minister says that it was necessary to have a continuous and timely exchange of information within the Ministry of the Interior in all lines of work in accordance with valid regulations and our earlier orders. In order to ensure that appropriate measures are taken, focusing on priorities, and providing specialist assistance, as well as informing the competent state organs. Then he says: "You shall report every day with reference to this order, on the execution of this order and problems that might occur in connection with performance of the tasks." This illustrates both the minister's and the ministry's position concerning insufficient communication and communication links; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you this: Do you recall that sometime in early August an employee of your administration together with a certain Drobok [phoen] from the national security service went to pick up mail in Bijeljina because telecom systems did not function, they were ambushed. Some were between Capard e and Zvornik where they unfortunately were killed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall the name of your employee in question? If you can't remember that, that's fine, but in any case he was a signals man in your administration, was he not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they both worked for me and then they were transferred to another service. I know the exact location. It was at Crni Vrh that they were ambushed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And as I said, it was in the first half of August 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember the exact date, but around that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have P668 shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: While we wait for the document to come up, Mr. Kezunovic, could I ask you if you ever attended any of the meetings with the minister, the daily meetings that you just referred to? Did you personally ever go to any of these meetings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These were not daily meetings. These were daily reports, information exchanged daily from the organs in the field, which would then be collated in the MUP headquarters and forwarded to operational services. I don't remember any meetings to that effect. Perhaps the minister did hold certain meetings if he believed the problem was important enough to have a meeting, such as the non-functioning of communications, then he might summon me to his office to explain. But this would only concern the most important things from those daily reports per professional line of work. I presume that if it did happen, it happened more frequently with other aspects of police work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I apologise because I understood that there were daily meetings held, but I was mistaken. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir -- could we only have the first page in Serbian and the second page in the English. Sir, this is a report of the SJB in Prijedor. On the first sheet, which in e-court in English is the second page, it says: "Coded dispatch return." I suppose this S with a diacritic is what you referred to when you explained it meant coded?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then we have the dates of the 18th and the 19th of July and the 1st of August. Can you explain this concept of "return." Does it mean that those coded dispatches were not sent?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that would be one of the options.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's have the first page in the English and second in the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you can see the third dispatch of the 1st of August here. Underlined we see the title "MUP of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and army of the Serbian Republic of B&H." And then there is a handwritten note saying: "We are not in a position to send it" or "we are unable to send it." This confirms what we have just said, that it was impossible to send it on the 1st of August?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I believe the note was made by the signals man.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So this Goran person?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. MR. ZECEVIC [Interpretation] Could we have P158 shown to the witness next.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: To further illustrate the situation with the CSB in Trebinje, the document you're about to see is a report on the work of the CSB in Trebinje between the 1st of July and the 15th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go to page 2, please. I suppose the same goes for both versions. Apologies. Page 3 then. In the English too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The third paragraph in both versions says: "Non-functional communications system, lack of equipment, and materiel, frequent fuel shortage, and interruption of communications, apart from insufficient number of workers, were special problem in performance of daily activities. As a result we are now unable to process data from the area of ancient Herzegovina, so this instruction only relates to the area of eastern Herzegovina." It is a fact, is it not, and you know that the CSB with its regional public security stations also had this issue of communications to deal with.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Much the same way as it was the case with the CSB in their communication with the communications centre at MUP headquarters at Pale; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All communication before that went through Mostar for the entire area of Herzegovina, and that was disrupted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It was disrupted because Mostar was controlled by Croatian or Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We see here that at the CSB they were unable to process information from a large part of the territory they covered?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The last document served to illustrate this issue has to do with the territory of the CSB in Doboj. You were shown this document yesterday, it is P1426. It is a report about the work of the communications department and encryption department of the CSB in Doboj between the 30th of July and the 30th of September, 1992. Head of department, Miomir Djekic signed it. You were shown this document yesterday and you recognised it, did you not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 it says that -- well, the date of the document is the 1st of October, 1992. It says: "In this period the employees of this technical services department managed to establish telephone and telegraph communication among the following liberated territories in the region: Derventa, Modrica, Teslic, Bosanski Samac, Petrovo, and Maglaj, although there are frequent disruptions in the communications with Maglaj and Petrovo ..." Based on this we can draw a certain conclusion, which is that the telephone and telegraph connections were not operational at least until the 30th of July concerning these municipalities, and between the 1st of August and the 30th of September communication was established. It was as late as that, was it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, although it was still under difficult circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Two paragraphs following that says that in the same period, between the 1st of August and the 1st of October, 1992, the CSB in Banja Luka was made part of the telephone and telegraph network, whereas the ministry could only be contacted through the KT or encryption system. It also states that towards the end of September communications were established between the CSB in Doboj and the CSB in Banja Luka and the ministry, and the ministry could only be reached by encrypted communication.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. But this should be interpreted in the way we saw a normal situation or what would amount to a normal situation in the sense of exchange of information by the regular means.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When I -- well, I'm talking about the regular system of communication within the Ministry of the Interior of the RS?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the last paragraph the department chief says that work is stabilised of the communications centre and the CSB since at the outset the system had been completely non-existent basically; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Sir, let's go back to the communications centre of the MUP. Could you please be shown P847. It is another document you saw yesterday. It is a fact that you had insufficient personnel, insufficient number of operators in the communications centre of the MUP headquarters at Pale; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Apologies. It could be that I was confused with the numbers. I wanted to see 65 ter 153. You remember this list, don't you, for personal incomes for May of the MUP headquarters?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, on page 2 we have a list of 12 names of people employed in the administration for communication, including you as assistant and head of the department, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, of these people here employed at the -- communications administration, a number of them -- I think you said three, I think you said that three of them were technicians; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just take a look. I can go through them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Andric Blagoje he worked in the PTT and he was an engineer and moved over to us. He was a graduate of engineering. And then the next person was for encryption. He was retired and reactivated. Vasilic Slobodan was also an engineer, having graduated from a higher -- the high school for PTT, and he worked in the municipal SUP. Then we have Dragan Elez. He was taken in later on. Predrag Bozic, also later on, which means that these two had no experience working in the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just pause there for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You were interested in who the technicians were; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in how many technicians you had and how many signals men you had.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, only three were operators, encoders, three of them. All the rest were technicians.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In fact, for you to be able to service the communications centre round the clock under normal conditions, you would need at least five people or six operators, signals men; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the lowest level in the communications centre at the security station, five; and of course far more for the MUP for anybody to be able to work round the clock, 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just a digression at this point, if I may. Yesterday you were asked several times by Mr. Hannis about the location at Pale, and you said that you were at a couple of locations at Pale, the centre, the communications centre. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the communications centre, but the MUP, the organs of this internal MUP unit. They were distributed in various facilities, and the communications centre would move around, although there was just one. It was one centre but moving around from one location to another.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sure you know, Mr. Kezunovic, that Mico Stanisic, as the minister, from June 1992 was at Jahorina not Pale.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I perhaps omitted to state that yesterday, but you're quite right. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, yesterday during our discussions, this communications centre at the Ministry of Defence was mentioned at Pale, do you remember that you spoke about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you also said on the same subject that a certain colonel, the late Milorad Kotlica, was in charge of that communications or signals detachment, which was the communication line for the government and other organs?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the assistant minister of defence for communications, just as I was for internal affairs he was for communications, and within that there was a detachment and the command of the detachment was a major, Redji Agic [phoen], I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Does the name Ranko Vukovic sound familiar? I think he worked in --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with the first and last name, but I can't link it up to an image. I don't know -- I can't remember how the man looked like, but yes, the name does ring a bell. I know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, please, this communications centre of the Ministry of Defence which served the government and the Presidency, did not have anything to do with the MUP; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not at the beginning, no. Not at that time, during the period that you're referring to, but later on I don't know what the fate of that centre and system was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What I want to say is that your communications centre, the one that you led as assistant minister and head of the department for communications and encryption in the MUP of Republika Srpska, was completely separate from this communications centre of the Ministry of Defence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you had your communications through your centre; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is a fact, is it not, that this communications centre of the Ministry of Defence also faced identical problems, the same problems you did, because it was linked up with the PTT system in the sphere of communication; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And it is also a fact, is it not, that they needed at least three months, or rather, over three months to establish any kind of communication at all from that centre?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, this morning you were discussing some documents with Mr. Hannis, and if I may -- well, if the OTP would return 1428 to you, please, so that you can have it in front of you to take a look at in hard copy, the printed version, please. If the Prosecution could help us out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: 65 ter 2516. [Interpretation] I apologise, I should have announced that earlier on, which I had omitted to do. Thank you, Mr. Hannis and Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's the document that you were asked to comment on by my learned friend. It's a notebook with entries of received and sent dispatches from the communications centre of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska for the period up to the 13th of May, I believe, 1992. And when that notebook was transferred to the centre in Sarajevo. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, it was put to you - and you accepted that - that although it says that this was a log-book of received and sent dispatches, that in actual fact the entries were for the most part -- or rather, that all the entries were of sent dispatches. And now I'd like us to look at number 20, which is on page 5 of the Serbian version, and I assume it's the same page in English. But anyway, let's look at number 20 in both versions. And there you will see that it was a dispatch received, a message of some kind, it says "message from Belgrade to the minister." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Then if we go on to number 36, the page with entry number 36, that's page 8, number 36, please. Once again, it's a dispatch received and it says: "SDS Ilidza information service," that's the person sending it. It's a report from -- some report from the military hospital, and so on. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So that's a dispatch received?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a moment ago and now I don't know what received message and received dispatch means. I can call up, for example, and say a brawl has broken out in a cafe. That would be information about something, somebody reporting something. This doesn't appear to be a dispatch to me, to be quite honest because if it is a proper dispatch then -- I don't know. It wouldn't say "dojava" or report. There would be a title of some sort, a heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, be that as it may, it doesn't only refer to sent dispatches but received dispatches as well. Let's take a look at the last page, number 49. Page 10. You've already looked at that page you will recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So the first document that we looked at under number 1 was of the 22nd of April, 1992, and this last one, number 49, is dated the 13th of May.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So that means a period of some three weeks overall. The entries cover a three-week period; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, for purposes of illustration and the lack of communication between the CBS of Doboj and Trebinje that we discussed earlier on, if you look at number 47 and number 48 you will see that there is no entry with the telephone when these were received in these SBS centres, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Doboj and Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the truth of the matter was that the communications were down, so these dispatches were never received; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, here we had the MUP headquarters, and the MUP has five SCBs, security services centres. Now, over the space of 21 days, which is the period covered here with the entries, we have barely 50, or rather, 49 dispatches sent out, which is I think about two and a half dispatches per day on average; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the maths of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, if you look, sir, at this log-book of received and sent dispatches, you will see that a certain number of dispatches - I mean more than ten - went to Pale within the ministry in its seat -- from Vrace to Pale?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that reduces the number of sent dispatches to other users towards the CBSs on the territory of Republika Srpska; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is the very beginning, April and May 1992. The security centre was just being established, there was a war on, and we have an average of two to two and a half dispatches a day if we count those moving within the ministry, within the ministry headquarters; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. The witness has testified before that dispatch has a certain meaning for him, and I think he's already indicated that he does not consider all of these things in this list as dispatches. So if we could clarify that with him. That's my only request.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm grateful to Mr. Hannis for his suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, when we leafed through this, and we have here among others under number 16, for example, on page 4 it says order and decision re: Stamps. Under number 16 that's what it says there. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Then we have, as we've already seen, under 20 some message. Then number 40, or rather, 36, report or information for "SRNA" and so on and so forth. So almost 50 per cent of these are not actually dispatches in the true sense of the word. So 50 documents listed here are not in fact dispatches in the true sense of the word, as we understand a dispatch and as it was used in the MUP of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So that then reduces the whole thing to barely one dispatch a day for the period from the 22nd of April to the 13th of May, 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, it comes out that way. It was the communications centre Vrace.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And "SRNA," where some of the reports went to, was in Pale, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So the traffic in those 21 days was - let me put it that way - mostly between Vrace and Pale; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please show the witness P1429, please. And I would kindly ask if the Prosecution has a hard copy of the document, if they could make the witness's job a little easier. Thank you. I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you saw this document and commented on it this morning, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: With the Prosecutor. This is a document that notes down outgoing mail, mail that is being sent from the MUP seat of -- the MUP of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And this refers to the period, as we can see here, from the 9th of November until the 30th of December, 1992. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And on the first page it says "dispatch," and then there are some documents. There are some accompanying documents, different documents that were sent out by the MUP at the Republika Srpska headquarters. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. But I keep thinking about one thing. When we had the previous document -- all right. But particularly this one, why are there no covers where it clearly states what that is, novel such and such written by so and so, published by such and such a publisher, so that you know clearly what this is. I am responding to questions about documents like this only because I am trying to be useful; but actually, it's very hard for me to talk about this because there used to be a public security centre in the Pale -- which was also located in Pale. Perhaps they also dispatched certain documents that also went through a certain route to reach somebody. So this can also create confusion, and these improvised log-books with different columns, different contents, where it says "sent" and "received," and so you're not sure whether it's one or the other. All of that can also be under a question mark -- well, I mean, I'm just making this observation. But I can continue to answer your questions in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you can see the dispatches on page 1 under 3 and 4 refer to an escort for the patriarch, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that the patriarch visited in late November 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember he did come at the end of the year, but I don't remember the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What is crucial as far as I'm concerned, sir, is this: This is 57 days in all from the 9th of November to the 30th of December -- 51 days. And we have a total of 97 outgoing dispatches and other documents from the ministry. At the end of the year there was an average of two dispatches a day that was sent out, more or less. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Still looking at this document, there is a log-book of incoming mail that covers the period of the 9th of November to the 31st of December, 1992. I don't know if Mr. Hannis perhaps has this document, a hard copy of the document for you to look at, Witness. The reference numbers where the document starts from are 0371-0760 and on. This is the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I've given him all that I have. I ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Hannis. [Interpretation] In order to make it easier for the witness, perhaps the usher can hand my copy over to him. I don't know if there is an English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can we have a 65 ter number, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that's the same -- that is the same 65 ter number, 65 ter 3218, which is P1429 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Oh, it's still -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But apparently this part of the document has not been translated. I wasn't aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] There's only a partial English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is something that I have noticed in relation to the previous document, and I noticed that and now I'm a little bit confused. That's why I wasn't really paying attention. In the first column behind the numerals, can we go back --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You're talking about the previous document that we were looking at?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please go back to the first page P1429, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Go ahead, sir, you wanted to comment.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The order number is in the first column and then let's look at the next column. You will notice that all the numbers there begin with a 10, 10-2, -3, -4, and all the way to the end, which means that this is not the number of the communications centre. This is the number of some organisational unit. And its documents are here which were sent, and you can see the numbers going up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So you are asserting that this document, P1429 that was shown to you by the Prosecution, is actually not a document of the communications centre of the Republika Srpska MUP?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not of the communications centre at all, because you would have the documents and dispatches that would be marked with different numbers, depending on the addressee or the person who was sending out the document. So this is what I have noticed. And that's why I made the remark. Why don't we have the cover for each of these log-books?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I assume that Mr. Hannis will cover that in his re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, please continue, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I just returned this document to me by Ms. Usher, but I think maybe the witness can comment on this because it appears to be different. Thank you very much. I'm really sorry. So the reference number is ERN 0371-0760. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, we have some different markings here, 02, 01, 01, then followed by 404 dash something, 143-11.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is exactly what I was remarking. This looks like a log-book of the communications centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. If that's what it seems to be to you, then let us comment on this one. Take your time and look.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But again, I don't see -- well, it does say that it's incoming mail log-book, but again it doesn't say whose log-book it is. This looks like the log-book of received dispatches.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It looks like a book of received dispatches of the communications centre attached to the Republika Srpska MUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. I'm interested if you can comment on the period from November 9th until the 31st of December. Can you please look at entry number 1 and can you look at the last entry, please. And it relates to 1992, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What is the last entry number?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is the log-book of incoming mail, and it covers all that arrived at the Republika Srpska MUP communications centre, regardless of whether it arrived from the security services centres, some other state organs, or third parties. Thus, everything that came in was noted in the log-book; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If we take it that at least one-half of those documents from the CSBs, if I manage to understand things and evaluate them correctly or two-thirds, and since we're talking about the period of 51 days again at the end of 1992 during war time, this again would mean at least -- at the most four dispatches from the CSBs on average reaching the MUP of Republika Srpska every day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's less than the total number of the CSBs, which is actually five?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct -- well, we have some from municipalities, from hospitals, institutions that have nothing to do with the MUP too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, can we now look at P625, please. You will recall and that you looked at this and commented on it with Mr. Hannis. This is the report on work in the period of April-December 1992. The date when the report was drafted is 1993. And you will recall that you told Mr. Hannis about the number of 9.585 ultra short connections achieved in that period in these nine months in 1992. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You gave us an explanation then that this number was extremely high and that it was indeed true; however, you also explained that these were only tests of connection, that there was no actual traffic using that backup system. You recall that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In this document, the report, it says that on average these tests were done on ultra short waves every 45 minutes; you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just to be perfectly clear, a test of connection looks like this: A calls B, B picks up, A reads out: Today's a nice day, B says: Received, over and out, and that's it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was a simple test of quality.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that's the explanation for this number, 9.585?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if that's a question, can we have an answer; if it's just a statement, can it be stricken.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe the witness answered. I don't know how it wasn't recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please repeat your answer to the last question. I said that's the explanation for this number, 9.585?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'll address it on re-direct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] That's page 29 -- or no, no, I'm sorry. 32 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 32 in Serbian, but I really can't find what page in English it is. It's FE20-1307.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the last-but-one paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm being told it's page 22 in English. It's the last-but-one -- no, no, it's on the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Kezunovic, but we have to get it on the screen. So in English it's paragraph 2 and in Serbian it's the last-but-one. It says: "On average 15 dispatches a day were sent to the centres and other organs of the interior from the MUP headquarters (a total of 4.170 in all lines of work) and on average 16 dispatches a day were received (a total of 4.400)."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Which means that in these nine months we have 9.585 [as interpreted] dispatches, both sent and received?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I suppose this is information attached by your administration to this report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't follow the math. 4.170 and 4.400 is not 9.585. I think you're referring to the old short wave number.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I said 8.570, and I believe --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm just reading what's on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I wasn't following the transcript. I was following the document. [Interpretation] Can we show the witness page 36 in Serbian, 27 in English. That's item 3. The tasks and duties of communication and cryptographic protection. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is part of this annual report, and in paragraph 1 -- first of all, your administration drafted this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we prepared a longer text. This was taken out of my overall report, and the analysis department took out the passages they believed relevant to the annual report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But you're not questioning this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, it's absolutely correct. We prepared it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I actually said you are not questioning the veracity of the data regarding your administration and you said "correct."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we maybe enlarge the first paragraph or I'll just read it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You say: "... it can be noted that this part of the Ministry of the Interior was among those which organisationally speaking faced the most problems."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KEZUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not that we had the most problems. We had only problems. You know what a problem is by definition, something you are not able to deal with; something you can deal with and resolve is not a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, don't forget to wind up in about three minutes for me, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Perhaps this is an adequate time for me to stop. I have maybe ten more minutes or 12, 15 for Monday morning. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Kezunovic. We'll continue on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Kezunovic, we're about to take the adjournment for the weekend and to resume at 9.00 on Monday. The Chamber will not rise immediately, so I'll ask the usher to escort you from the chamber. We trust you have a safe weekend. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the bulletins tendered at the end of the previous session will be assigned numbers P1430 through P1445, and the 17th document is already marked for identification as P142, so it will be admitted as exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry. On the 28th of May, 2010, the Prosecution filed a motion to amend its Rule 65 ter witness list as a result of the Trial Chamber's decision of the 1st of April, 2010, on judicial notice of adjudicated facts, seeking to add 57 witnesses. The Defence jointly responded on the 8th of June, 2010, objecting to the motion, in part on the ground of incomplete disclosure of witness material pursuant to Rule 66(A)(ii). To consider a motion for additional witnesses once the trial has commenced, the Chamber must be satisfied, inter alia, that the anticipated testimony of each proposed witness is relevant and probative to the issues in the case and that the Defence has adequate time to prepare its cross-examination and is not unduly prejudiced by the decision -- by the addition. Accordingly, the Chamber would have expected the Prosecution to provide the summaries of the anticipated testimony of the proposed 57 witnesses pursuant to Rule 65 ter (E)(ii) (b) in a contemporaneous filing. In the absence of these summaries not yet provided, the Chamber is unable to proceed with the motion on the merits. Further, the Prosecution's motion does not inform the Chamber of the progress it has made in fulfilling the disclosure obligation under Rule 66(A)(ii) for the proposed witnesses since it formed the intention to call them. For these reasons, the Chamber now orders the Prosecution to file an addendum with the summaries of the anticipated evidence of the proposed 57 witnesses by Wednesday, the 16th of June. The Chamber also orders the Prosecution to provide status reports on the disclosure of material related to the proposed additional witnesses pursuant to Rule 66(A)(ii). So we take the adjournment to Monday morning, and I believe according to the schedule we're in Courtroom III for all mornings next week. So I trust everyone has a safe weekend. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 14th day of June, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.
